newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada beef exports up despite sluggish '96 demand.
newsitem.headline: Canada beef exports up despite sluggish '96 demand.

text.p: Canadian beef exports to key Asian and Mexican markets rose in 1996 despite "sluggish" demand due to quality, a Canada Beef Export Federation official said.
"Market share increases were hard won as the demand for beef in Asia and Mexico was sluggish in 1996," Canada Beef Export Federation president Jim Graham said in a statement Tuesday.
Canadian beef and veal product exports to Asia were up 22 percent in volume and 11 percent in value in 1996 and Mexican exports were up three percent in volume and 22 percent in value.
"These results confirm...that long-term export opportunities exist for our high quality beef and veal in Asia," Graham said.
CBEF is an industry based market development agency.

Canada exported 22.7 million kgs (50.1 million lbs) of beef and veal valued at C$113.3 million to Asia in 1996. Exports to Mexico were 3.1 million kgs (6.8 million lbs) of beef and veal priced at C$4.587 million, Agriculture Canada figures show.
"The Canadian cattle and beef industry is well on its way to achieving its export goals for the year 2000," CBFE executive director Ted Haney said in the statement.
Sales would need to rise 49 percent in the next four years to achieve CBEF's goal of 115 million kgs (253.5 million lbs) to Asian and Mexican markets by 2000.
"Our industry will reach its goal to export beef and veal products equivalent to 690,000 fed cattle to Asia and Mexico by the end of 2000," CBFE president Graham said.
